title: Special resolution to re-register a private company as public
ruleSource: Written from S.A Badmus' Corporate Law drafts (Lawdeck knowledge base). To be confirmed by the legal reviewer, including every section of the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020 cited.

parts.why: Company documents carry the company's name, registered address and registration (RC) number, and for resolutions and notices the statutory heading. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.text: SPECIAL RESOLUTION FOR THE RE-REGISTRATION OF {{companyName}} AS A PUBLIC COMPANY PURSUANT TO {{provision}}
parts.why: The title and the provision of CAMA relied on. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.text:
At the general meeting of the company held on {{meetingDate}} at {{meetingPlace}}, the following resolutions were proposed and duly passed as special resolutions:
#. That, subject to the consent of the Corporate Affairs Commission, the company be re-registered as a public company limited by shares by the name of {{newName}}.
#. That the consequential alterations be made in the memorandum and articles of association of the company to reflect its re-registration.
parts.why: The resolutions: re-registration subject to the Commission's consent, the new name (ending 'Plc'), and consequential alterations to the memorandum and articles. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

Resolutions are dated and signed, usually by two directors or a director and the secretary. Always sign and date in the exam, on or before the exam date. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
